root_cause.text: In NFSD's `nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg()`, the `nfs4_file` read-file pointers and access counts were mismanaged by overwriting `fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY]` without dropping any existing `nfsd_file` reference and by assigning the same `nfsd_file` to both `fi_fds[O_RDONLY]` and `fi_rdeleg_file` with only one reference, causing leaked/orphaned references when READ opens already existed.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that `nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg()` "unconditionally overwrites `fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY]` ... without releasing its reference" and "stored the same `nfsd_file` pointer in both `fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY]` and `fp->fi_rdeleg_file` with only a single reference"; the patch fixes this by only setting `fi_fds[O_RDONLY]` if it is NULL, taking a separate `nfsd_file_get()` for `fi_rdeleg_file`, and adding `nfsd_file_put(rnf)` in `put_deleg_file()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix delegation file cleanup by releasing `rnf` and only dropping read access when a read delegation file actually exists.
intent_record.what: The change adds braces around the `if (rnf)` block in `put_deleg_file()` and moves the existing `nfs4_file_put_access(fp, NFS4_SHARE_ACCESS_READ);` call inside that conditional, while also adding a new `nfsd_file_put(rnf);` call before it.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the read delegation file reference `rnf` is now released with `nfsd_file_put(rnf)` when it exists, and the corresponding read access count is decremented only in that same case. This prevents dropping read access when no read delegation file was present and fixes a missing release of the `rnf` file reference.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix read-delegation file handling to avoid clobbering an existing read-only file entry and to maintain correct nfsd_file reference ownership.
intent_record.what: Within nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg(), the code that unconditionally assigned nf to fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] and fp->fi_rdeleg_file was replaced with logic under fp->fi_lock that only stores nf into fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] if that slot is empty, sets nf to NULL after transferring ownership, and then assigns fp->fi_rdeleg_file from nfsd_file_get(fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY]); after releasing the lock, the code now conditionally calls nfsd_file_put(nf) if nf was not consumed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents overwriting an existing O_RDONLY file descriptor entry, ensures fi_rdeleg_file always holds a referenced copy of the file actually stored in fi_fds[O_RDONLY], and correctly drops the extra reference when a new nf is not installed, avoiding reference leaks and preserving consistent shared state under locking.

grouping_result.intent: Fix read-delegation file handling to avoid clobbering an existing read-only file entry and to maintain correct nfsd_file reference ownership.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix read-delegation file lifecycle and reference management so existing read-only file entries are preserved and cleanup only releases or drops access when a corresponding read delegation file actually exists.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause: they fix incorrect read-delegation file reference/lifecycle handling, avoid overwriting an existing O_RDONLY entry, and ensure cleanup/access drops only occur when a real read-delegation file exists.

candidates.rationale: This directly overwrites any existing read-only nfsd_file pointer in fi_fds[O_RDONLY] without first dropping the prior reference, which is the core mismanagement causing leaked/orphaned references when READ opens already exist.

This stores the same nfsd_file in the read-delegation slot after assigning it to fi_fds[O_RDONLY], but without taking a separate reference, so two owners alias one referenced object and cleanup/accounting become inconsistent.

Pre-fix cleanup dropped read access merely based on rnf being non-NULL, reflecting the incorrect lifecycle model around the read delegation file and contributing to mismatched access/reference handling.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the primary vulnerable assignment: it overwrites the existing read-only nfsd_file pointer slot without first releasing any prior referenced object, directly causing the leaked/orphaned reference condition when a READ open already exists.

This assigns the same nfsd_file object to a second ownership slot after fi_fds[O_RDONLY] is set, but without taking an additional reference. That creates two logical owners backed by only one reference, leading to inconsistent cleanup and access/reference accounting.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant vulnerable logic directly in `nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg()`. In the added code at the bottom, while holding `fp->fi_lock`, it does `__nfs4_file_get_access(fp, NFS4_SHARE_ACCESS_READ);`, then assigns `fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] = nf;` and `fp->fi_rdeleg_file = nf;`. It does not fix the underlying mismanagement inside `nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg()` itself: the overwrite of `fi_fds[O_RDONLY]` remains, and no additional `nfsd_file` reference is taken for storing `nf` in both fields. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the function does not already contain the full fix.
